8z52zk:285: These scenarios share common characteristics: they are extremely sensitive to disk IOPS/latency, and rely on application-layer multi-replication (such as Kafka's Replication Factor, Kvrocks primary-replica replication) to ensure data reliability, so the temporary nature of a single-node Instance Store is acceptable. However, in the stage of single-AZ deployment or multi-replication not yet fully ready, once the instance lifecycle is unexpectedly interrupted (stop, terminate, migration), the data on Instance Store will be lost immediately and irreversibly. In modern cloud operations, the ways to interrupt an instance lifecycle far exceed our intuition — not only human misoperation, but also system-automated actions such as Auto Recovery, ASG scale-in, and Karpenter node consolidation.
